Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Raleigh NC
215 PM EDT Sun Sep 6 2026

.DISCUSSION...
As of 215 PM Sunday...

Aloft, the ~594 dam mid-level anticyclone to the west to start the 
week will strengthen and build ewd across the region by mid-week. 
The trough associated with a potent nrn stream system tracking 
across cntl and ern Canada should amplify swd, then progress ewd 
across the region mid to late week. This trough should help push the 
anticyclone wwd and out of the area before it builds in over the 
weekend once again. At the surface, high pressure will slide sewd 
across the mid-Atlantic, shifting offshore by Tue night. The high 
may continue to ridge into the area on Wed, however a warm front 
should lift nwd across the area Wed night/Thu as the pre-frontal 
trough sets up, with sly-swly flow expected Thu-Fri. The cold front 
should approach from the north on Fri, however its progression into 
the area remains uncertain at this time. While diurnal convection is 
possible each day, the highest chances will be Thu/Fri ahead of the 
front. High temperatures to start the week should be in the low to 
mid 80s, moderating through Thu, when highs in the upper 80s to low 
90s are expected.

FXUS62 KRAH 070701
AFDRAH

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Raleigh NC
300 AM EDT Mon Sep 7 2026

.DISCUSSION...
As of 300 AM Monday...

As the upper ridge continues to flatten, we'll eventually see a 
longwave trough and attendant surface cold front move out of the 
Ohio Valley and into the Mid Atlantic/Southeast late in the week. As 
such we'll see increasing shower and storm chances as early as 
Thursday afternoon within an increasingly unstable pre-frontal 
airmass. There is still some uncertainty with respect to when the 
front/trough will move through NC (most ensemble guidance suggests 
Friday vs Thursday night), but we'll continue to maintain increased 
PoPs through the day Friday given ensemble support. That said the 
strongest forcing for ascent associated with the trough should be 
displaced well north of NC and it remains to be seen just how much 
QPF is realized with the front when it arrives.
